guarantees.claim: For each share index i, always_comb assigns encoded_key[i] based on key_len_i: Key128 → {(8+MaxKeyLen-128)'(0), key_data_i[i][0+:128], encode_keylen[i][0+:MaxEncodedKeyLenSize]}; Key192 → {(8+MaxKeyLen-192)'(0), key_data_i[i][0+:192], encode_keylen[i][0+:MaxEncodedKeyLenSize]}; Key256 → {(MaxKeyLen-256)'(0), key_data_i[i][0+:256], encode_keylen[i]}; Key384 → {(MaxKeyLen-384)'(0), key_data_i[i][0+:384], encode_keylen[i]}; Key512 → {key_data_i[i][0+:512], encode_keylen[i]} (assumes MaxKeyLen=512); default → '0.

assumptions.claim: Parameter MaxKeyLen must be exactly 512; the Key512 branch omits padding under the assumption that 512 is the maximum key length.
assumptions.risk: If MaxKeyLen > 512, the Key512 concatenation will be narrower than other branches and may not match the declared width of encoded_key[i], causing unintended zero-extension or truncation.

assumptions.claim: key_len_i must be one of the five legal values (Key128/192/256/384/512) for the encoded key to carry meaningful data; any other value results in encoded_key[i]=0.
assumptions.cond: when key_len_i is used to drive the case
assumptions.risk: An illegal key_len_i causes an all‑zero encoded key, which may be fed to the SHA‑3 core, potentially bypassing key‑length integrity checks and weakening security.

assumptions.claim: key_data_i[i] must be at least MaxKeyLen bits wide, and encode_keylen[i] must be at least MaxEncodedKeyLenSize bits wide.
assumptions.risk: Under‑sized inputs would cause X‑propagation or synthesis errors.

uncertain_points.claim: The unique case default silently forces encoded_key[i] to all zeros when key_len_i does not match any listed key length. It is not clear whether this is intentional (safe‑state) or should trigger an error/alert to prevent zero‑key processing.
uncertain_points.risk: An attacker or a software fault could select an unhandled key length, resulting in an all‑zero encoded key that bypasses key‑length integrity checks and may lead to SHA‑3 processing with a weak key.

uncertain_points.claim: The Key512 branch does not include zero‑padding, explicitly assuming MaxKeyLen = 512. If MaxKeyLen is parameterized to another value, the concatenation width may differ from the other branches, potentially causing width mismatch or truncation.
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect key encoding width could propagate to downstream logic and produce wrong operational behavior.

uncertain_points.claim: The unique case enumerates only five key length constants; it is unknown whether the key_len_i enum contains additional legal values that are intentionally omitted or whether the design supports only these five lengths.
uncertain_points.cond: if key_len_i takes an undefined enum member
uncertain_points.risk: Missing legal cases would silently fall into default and produce an all‑zero encoded key, altering the cryptographic operation without detection.
